images.caption:
By the 1880s the Brunner mine was producing more coal than any other in New Zealand.

The site is well known for this country’s greatest mining tragedy in 1896 when 65 workers died following a gas and coal dust explosion. A memorial to the disaster, erected for the centennial commemoration, is located on the site, along with ruins of coal-mining and coke making structures.

Monuments and memorials in West Coast Region

images.caption: Stillwater is a timber mill settlement and railway station on the line across Arthur's Pass, beside the Grey River. The Stillwater Cemetery contains a memorial to the victims of the nearby Brunner Mine disaster of 1896, and mass grave of 33 of the victims.
images.alt: Stillwater is a timber mill settlement and railway station on the line across Arthur's Pass, beside the Grey River. The Stillwater Cemetery contains a memorial to the victims of the nearby Brunner Mine disaster of 1896, and mass grave of 33 of the victims.

images.caption: The coal mine at Brunner on the Grey River, West Coast, was New Zealand's largest. It was the site of New Zealand's largest mine disaster, when 65 men were killed in a mine explosion in 1896. Today it is the site of a restored heritage area, and has memorials to the victims of the explosion and to the Pike River disaster.
